Defective bone mineralization defines this metabolic disorder; pulmonary hypoplasia from severe thoracic underdevelopment commonly (>30%) contributes to lethal respiratory failure.
Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor arising in the jejunum; neuroendocrine histology alone does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Squamous cell carcinoma arising in the ureter.
Preeclampsia is defined by pregnancy-associated hypertension with proteinuria or other organ dysfunction; renal endothelial injury is characteristic.
Protozoal infection umbrella; affected anatomical organs vary substantially among its constituent infections.
Craniosynostosis and hallucal skeletal defects, together with ocular abnormalities, define the syndrome.
Childhood astrocytic neoplasm arises from nervous system glial tissue.
Developmental delay in 9/19; individual cardiac and renal lesions are below 30%, and overlapping counts do not establish a common aggregate organ involvement rate.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration with visual impairment; IDH3B causation alone does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Minimally invasive adenocarcinoma arising in the lung.
Autoimmune overlap disease directly affects liver and bile ducts; colitis is occasional and separately diagnosed, and pruritus does not establish skin damage.
Malignant neoplasm occupying the renal pelvis.
Neoplasm of the adrenal medulla, an endocrine gland compartment; cardiovascular injury is not universal across this tumor umbrella.
Meningeal tumor in the suprasellar region; optic nerve or chiasmal compression causes visual dysfunction in most symptomatic patients (>50%).
Benign neoplasm located in the large intestine.
CNS hemosiderin toxicity causes defining cerebellar degeneration and progressive sensorineural hearing loss; bleeding does not establish a systemic coagulation disorder.
Halothane hepatitis is characteristically immune-mediated hepatic injury triggered by halothane exposure.
Isolated bilateral cerebellar malformation causes motor, cognitive and language dysfunction.
Combined immunodeficiency defines the umbrella; infections and secondary anatomical damage vary among subtypes.
Inherited triglyceride metabolism disorder; atherosclerosis and pancreatitis are separate complications, and damaging skin involvement is not established as common.
Adenocarcinoma of the uterine cervix; reproductive organs have no axis, and no other common direct organ involvement is established.
Intellectual disability defines the syndrome; kyphoscoliosis occurs in 3/3 and scoliosis is frequent; dental malocclusion affects 2/3, supporting gastrointestinal involvement.
Ulcerated lesion directly damages the esophageal wall; an infectious or autoimmune mechanism is not inherent to this umbrella.
Inherited lipoprotein metabolism disorder with defining glomerular lipoprotein deposition, proteinuria and renal dysfunction.
